## 3. The evidence that moved it














**Three negative checkpoint phase 3s in one month, and only one of them is about
a new target.** [BR.31](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41529222/) finds no disease-free survival benefit for
adjuvant durvalumab in resected NSCLC at any PD-L1 level (stratified hazard ratio
0.93, P = .64, at 60 months' median follow-up);
[KEYVIBE-010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41698381/) finds no recurrence-free survival benefit from adding
anti-TIGIT to pembrolizumab as adjuvant melanoma therapy; and
[LU005](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41529214/) finds no survival benefit from adding atezolizumab to
chemoradiation in limited-stage small-cell lung cancer (median overall survival
36.1 versus 31.1 months, hazard ratio 1.03). All three are the same design move —
take an agent that works in advanced disease and push it earlier or add it to a
backbone — and all three fail. The adjuvant setting is where this corpus should
now expect checkpoint combinations to fail by default.

The distinction that had been collapsed here is worth keeping. Durvalumab and
atezolizumab are PD-L1 blockade: BR.31 and LU005 test the existing generation in
new settings, and however clean their nulls are they cannot bear in either
direction on a claim about targets *beyond* PD-1 and CTLA-4. Both cards are now
neutral on `next-gen-checkpoints`, and KEYVIBE-010 is the one of the three that
actually reads out on a second-generation target.

**A target was killed by a reagent artifact.** [41871876](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41871876/) (*JITC*)
reports that the high BCMA expression reported in AML is an artifact of
nonspecific Fc binding, and that anti-BCMA CAR-T barely lyses AML cells. This is
the most economical refutation in the corpus: one antibody-validation control
removes an entire proposed indication for a platform that already works
elsewhere.

**Agentic AI produced three genuine supports in a single month.**
[MOSAIC](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41554982/) trains 2,498 specialised chemical experts on millions of
reaction protocols and returns executable synthesis protocols at a 71% success
rate, with experimental realisation of more than 35 new compounds and reaction
methodology that was absent from the experts' training; an
[agentic system for rare-disease diagnosis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41708847/) carries traceable,
auditable reasoning; and [LUMI-lab](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41742414/), a foundation-model-driven
autonomous platform, discovers ionizable lipid chemistry. Two features are worth
separating. MOSAIC's number is wet-lab validated rather than benchmark-scored,
which is rare on this thread. And the rare-disease system's selling point is that
its reasoning can be checked rather than that it works — a different kind of
claim from the rest of the thread, and the one that would survive a sceptical
reader.

**Vaccines reached unaffected people.** [41545594](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41545594/) tests the
Nous-209 shared-frameshift-neoantigen vaccine in *unaffected* Lynch syndrome
carriers, and [41818359](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41818359/) (*Science*) reframes KRAS inhibition as
prevention in precursor lesions rather than treatment of advanced disease. Both
sit at the join between `neoantigen-vaccines` and `interception`, and both move
the intervention point earlier than any trial this corpus has previously
recorded.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This subsection carried [41512868](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41512868/)
    as a refutation. The finding is unchanged and the reading below still holds,
    but what the paper contradicts is a background assumption about B cells, not
    a claim this corpus tracks. What it demonstrates — lymphoid-structure
    integrity governing immunotherapy response, and made druggable — is the
    `neuro-immune-microbiome-axis` claim itself, and the card now reads
    `supports`. It was recorded against the thread it evidences.

[41512868](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41512868/) (*Cancer Cell*): an IGLL5-positive B cell subset in
bladder cancer binds high endothelial venules through IGLL5-LTβR, inhibiting
non-canonical NF-κB signalling and *disassembling* tertiary lymphoid structures,
which impairs immunotherapy response in genetically engineered and humanised
mice; blocking IGLL5 preserves the structures and improves immunotherapy in
patient-derived xenograft and pan-cancer models. TLS have been treated across
this corpus as a favourable feature to induce, and the B cell compartment as
what builds them. Together with the September 2025 finding that Treg- and
MDSC-rich TLS mark fatal cervical cancer, the position now is that TLS presence
is not a biomarker and TLS induction is not obviously a goal — what matters is
which cells are in them, and here that is a specific subset with a ligand that
can be blocked.

### (b) Method credibility

[40790276](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40790276/) (*Nat Biomed Eng*): latent diffusion models memorize
patient imaging data, so synthetic medical images are not privacy-preserving.
This is filed under method credibility rather than foundation models on purpose —
it is not a capability limit, it is a claim that a stated property of a deployed
technique is false.

[41772176](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41772176/): histology-based molecular biomarker models learn
clinicopathological confounders rather than molecular state. Read against
[41372473](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41372473/) from December — foundation models in oncology win
benchmarks and miss the clinic — this supplies the mechanism for the miss.

[41763219](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41763219/) (*Cell Syst*): CRISPRa activation levels are confounded
by shared cellular resources rather than by guide or target biology. Every
CRISPRa screen that reads activation strength as a biological quantity inherits
this.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This subsection carried
    [41653917](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41653917/) as evidence that prior
    cfDNA end-motif and fragmentomic analyses used partial end representations
    and so biased published classifiers, and read it as the "second consecutive
    month with a cfDNA-classifier artifact, after February's demographic-bias
    card". Neither half survives the abstracts. This paper is a method advance,
    not an audit: 3' ends were overlooked because standard protocols modify
    them, and single-stranded "2-end" and "4-end" sequencing recovers the native
    motifs and detects hepatocellular carcinoma at AUC 0.95, rising to 0.97 with
    3' fragmentomic methylation. It makes no claim about published classifiers.
    February's card was also misread — see that month — so there was no
    two-month run to name. The card is now neutral, filed on `ctdna-mrd` as a
    new modality rather than here.
